subject: astronomy
title: Day, Night & Seasons: Weather Patterns
welcome_lead: Tilt changes how much heat each part of Earth gets — and that drives the weather.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: temperature, daylight hours, weather links.
final_note: Heat from the Sun varies all year — your jacket choice depends on it.

concepts.def: The usual weather of a place over years.
How hot or cold something is.
How far north or south you are.
Line around Earth's middle — equal day/night.
Top or bottom of Earth's axis.

walkthroughs.body_html: Near the equator, the Sun is high all year and days stay close to 12 hours. Near the poles, summers have 24-hour daylight and winters have 24-hour night.
In London in summer the day can be 16 hours. In winter it can be under 8 hours. Closer to the poles, the swing is even bigger.
Weather changes daily. Climate is the long-term average. The same tilt that gives seasons also shapes Earth's climate zones.
